brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Evocative metaphor — constellations as series with glow states create instant emotional pull and reflective intrigue
Restrained palette of midnight blue, emerald, and amber reads cohesively and maps cleanly to status semantics
Player chrome is quiet and defers to the star map, letting the conceptual canvas dominate the screen
dominant_weaknesses: Constellations lack labels, titles, or hover affordances — users can't identify a series or episode without trial clicking
Connecting lines feel arbitrary; many dots drift untethered, breaking the 'pattern' promise of the brief
Spatial layout has no hierarchy or anchor — every cluster competes equally, making navigation overwhelming at scale
fix_priorities: Add series names anchored to each constellation cluster with subtle typographic labels
Strengthen line logic so each series forms a recognizable shape, not scattered noise
Introduce hover/focus states revealing episode metadata to bridge metaphor and utility
Tighten typography scale in the player bar — title and show name need stronger weight contrast
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective appeal from the metaphor, but behavioral usability collapses without labels, grouping cues, or interaction affordances.
rationale.intent_fit: It captures the poetic premise beautifully but underdelivers on 'series form patterns' since clusters read as random scatter rather than legible constellations.
